items.title: The Last Bus Home
items.text: The bus smelled exactly as it had twenty years ago: warm vinyl, old coins, and rain on wool coats. I pressed my forehead against the window and watched the bakery, the tiny cinema, and the crooked fence of my old school slide past. Everything seemed smaller now, as if the town had quietly shrunk while I was away. At the corner of Pine Street, a boy in a yellow raincoat jumped over a puddle, and for a moment I was him, racing home for dinner with a bag of marbles in my pocket. I smiled, though my eyes stung. The driver called out my stop. I stayed seated for one more block, not ready to let the memory end.

qs.q: Which word best describes the mood of the passage?
o: Furious
Wistful
Indifferent
Alarmed
qs.why: 옛 기억을 그리워하는 쓸쓸하고 애틋한 분위기예요. 웃으면서도 눈이 시린 점이 단서예요.

qs.q: Why does the narrator say the town "seemed smaller"?
o: Seen with adult eyes after many years away, familiar places look less grand.
Many buildings along the route have recently been pulled down to make room.
The bus is moving too fast for the narrator to notice any details.
Most of the townspeople have moved out since the narrator last visited.
qs.why: 오랜만에 어른의 눈으로 보니 어릴 적 장소가 작게 느껴진다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "for a moment I was him" suggest?
o: The narrator once met the boy on the same street corner.
The narrator is acting out a role in a school play.
The narrator is jealous of the boy's new yellow raincoat and his bag of marbles.
The sight of the boy brought back the narrator's own childhood.
qs.why: 소년을 보고 자신의 어린 시절이 떠올랐다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does the narrator stay seated for one more block?
o: The narrator has forgotten which stop is the right one.
The narrator is waiting for the rain outside to stop.
The narrator wants to hold on to the feeling a little longer.
The narrator is afraid of getting off in front of the driver.
qs.why: 추억이 끝나는 것이 아쉬워 조금 더 머무르고 싶은 심정이에요.

items.title: Notice to Library Members
items.text: Notice to All Library Members. As of Monday, 3 March, the reading room on the second floor will be closed for repairs to the ceiling and lighting. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and thank you for your patience during this period. Members who wish to study quietly may use the tables near the main entrance, which will remain open during regular hours. Books reserved from the second floor can be collected at the front desk upon request. The work is expected to be completed by the end of April. Further updates will be posted on our website and at the entrance. Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to speak with a member of staff, who will be glad to assist you.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this notice?
o: To ask members to donate money for repairs to the building
To tell members about a temporary closure and what they can use instead
To invite members to a ceremony for the new lighting system
To warn members that overdue books will be charged a fine
qs.why: 임시 휴관 사실과 대안을 알리는 안내문이에요.

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone of the notice?
o: Courteous and formal
Casual and humorous
Stern and threatening
Excited and boastful
qs.why: apologize, thank, please, glad to assist 등 정중하고 격식 있는 표현이 쓰였어요.

qs.q: Where can members study quietly during the repairs?
o: In the second-floor reading room
In the offices behind the front desk
At tables outside the library building
At the tables near the main entrance
qs.why: 출입구 근처 탁자는 정상 운영 시간에 이용할 수 있다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the repairs?
o: They have already been finished for several weeks.
They will be over by the end of the same week.
They are expected to last for about two months.
They will continue until the end of the year.
qs.why: 3월 3일부터 4월 말까지이므로 약 두 달이에요.

items.title: Waiting for the Results
items.text: Dara refreshed the page for the ninth time. Nothing but a spinning circle. Her stomach felt like a washing machine, and every tick of the kitchen clock seemed unusually loud. Three months of late-night studying had come down to a single number on a screen. She tried to read a magazine, but the words kept sliding away. Her brother walked in, took one look at her, and set a cup of tea beside her laptop without a word. "It will be what it will be," he said gently. Dara nodded, but her fingers still trembled above the keyboard. Then the page loaded. She closed her eyes, counted to three, and slowly opened one of them.

qs.q: Which word best describes the mood of the passage?
o: Cheerful
Nervous
Peaceful
Hostile
qs.why: 초조하게 결과를 기다리는 긴장된 분위기예요.

qs.q: What does "Her stomach felt like a washing machine" mean?
o: She was so anxious that her insides seemed to be churning.
She had eaten food that did not agree with her at dinner.
She was bored and thought about doing household chores.
She was feeling hungry because she had skipped both lunch and dinner that day.
qs.why: 비유 표현으로, 불안해서 속이 울렁거린다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the brother's behavior show?
o: He is annoyed that she has used the laptop for so long.
He is curious to see the result before his sister does.
He believes that she has not studied enough to succeed.
He is caring and knows that quiet support helps more than advice.
qs.why: 말없이 차를 두고 가는 행동은 배려심을 보여 줘요.

qs.q: Why does Dara open only one eye at the end?
o: She has something stuck in her eye after the long wait.
She wants to read the screen slowly from a safer distance so that she can avoid mistakes.
She is afraid of what the number on the screen might be.
She is trying to hide the result from her brother.
qs.why: 결과가 두려워 한쪽 눈만 뜨는 거예요.

items.title: Review: The Quiet Cup
items.text: I went to The Quiet Cup expecting very little, so I was surprised to find myself staying for three hours. The room is small, with mismatched chairs, soft lamps, and a shelf of worn paperbacks that customers are invited to borrow. The coffee was good, though not remarkable, and the sandwich was a little dry. Still, none of that mattered much. The owner greeted every customer by name and refilled my water without being asked. If you want a flawless menu, look elsewhere. But if you need a corner where a rainy afternoon feels like a gift, this is the place. I left with a borrowed novel and a lighter heart, already planning my next visit.

qs.q: What is the writer's overall attitude toward the café?
o: Strongly negative because of poor service
Warmly positive despite a few minor faults
Completely neutral, like a plain news report
Mildly bored by the quiet atmosphere
qs.why: 음식의 작은 흠을 인정하면서도 전반적으로 애정 어린 평가예요.

qs.q: What does the writer mean by "none of that mattered much"?
o: The weak points of the food were outweighed by the pleasant atmosphere.
The coffee and the sandwich were exactly what the writer had hoped for.
The writer did not notice the taste of anything during the visit.
The writer would never return because the problems were too serious.
qs.why: 음식의 단점보다 분위기와 서비스의 장점이 더 컸다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Who is the review mainly meant for?
o: Chefs who want to learn how to cook better sandwiches
Owners who are looking to sell their cafés quickly
Travelers who need a cheap place to sleep overnight
Readers who value a cozy, relaxing place over a perfect menu
qs.why: "If you need a corner..."에서 독자가 어떤 사람인지 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which of the following is stated in the passage?
o: The sandwiches are the best feature of the café.
The owner charges extra for refilling water glasses.
Customers may borrow books from the café's shelf.
The café has comfortable matching armchairs.
qs.why: 책을 빌릴 수 있다고 직접 언급했어요.

items.title: Plant a Tree Today
items.text: Every autumn, our town loses dozens of old trees to roadwork and new buildings. We rarely notice, because the change is slow, but the consequences are not. Summer streets are several degrees hotter than before, and the birds that once woke us each morning have grown quiet. If we continue like this, our grandchildren will inherit a town of glass and concrete. The solution, however, is surprisingly simple. A young tree costs less than a restaurant meal, and it will cool, clean, and shelter for fifty years. Next Saturday, the council is giving away seedlings at the park gate. Come with a spade and a friend. Waiting for someone else to act is the one choice we cannot afford.

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
o: To report the results of a scientific experiment on heat
To persuade residents to take part in planting trees
To entertain readers with a story about birds
To advertise a restaurant that sells cheap meals
qs.why: 마지막 부분에서 행동을 촉구하는 설득문이에요.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes the tone of the passage?
o: Concerned but encouraging
Mocking and careless
Calm and completely detached
Angry and hopeless
qs.why: 문제를 우려하면서도 해결 가능하다고 독려하는 어조예요.

qs.q: What does "the one choice we cannot afford" imply?
o: Planting trees is too expensive for most families.
Only wealthy citizens can choose to help the town.
The council has decided to stop giving away seedlings at the park gate next Saturday.
Doing nothing would cost the town more than acting now.
qs.why: 아무 행동도 하지 않는 것이 가장 큰 손해라는 함축이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what has happened because trees were removed?
o: Roadwork has become cheaper for the council.
The park gate has been closed to visitors.
Summer streets have become hotter and fewer birds sing.
Restaurant meals have become more expensive.
qs.why: 더워진 거리와 줄어든 새소리가 언급돼요.

qs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to "inherit" in the passage?
o: Purchase something from a shop in town
Receive from earlier generations
Borrow for a short time
Destroy completely
qs.why: inherit는 앞 세대로부터 물려받는다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Two Hundred Meters to Go
items.text: My legs had stopped listening somewhere around kilometer thirty. All I could hear was my own breathing and the thin, steady rhythm of my shoes on the road. Then I turned the final corner, and the sound hit me like a wave: thousands of strangers shouting my name from the barriers, waving signs and ringing bells. Two hundred meters. My eyes blurred, but not from sweat. I thought of the cold mornings, the blisters, the evenings when I had wanted to quit. A woman held out a paper cup as I passed, her face shining, and I realized I was laughing out loud. When I crossed the line, I did not feel tired at all. I felt as if I could fly.

qs.q: How does the narrator feel at the end of the race?
o: Overjoyed and proud
Disappointed and bored
Ashamed and worried
Calm and uninterested
qs.why: 웃음과 날 것 같은 기분은 기쁨과 자부심을 나타내요.

qs.q: What changes in the mood between the first and last parts?
o: From fear to anger
From laughter to sadness
From curiosity to boredom
From exhaustion to excitement
qs.why: 지친 상태에서 환호 속의 고양감으로 바뀌어요.

qs.q: Why does the narrator's vision blur?
o: Sweat is running down the narrator's forehead and into both of the narrator's eyes.
The narrator has been hit by a flying sign.
Strong emotion has filled the narrator's eyes with tears.
The narrator is dizzy from the early morning cold.
qs.why: "but not from sweat"라고 해서 감정 때문이라는 걸 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does "the sound hit me like a wave" emphasize?
o: How cold the weather had turned near the finish
How overwhelming and powerful the cheering was
How many bells were broken along the road
How far the sea was from the race course
qs.why: 응원 소리의 압도적인 힘을 비유한 표현이에요.

items.title: A Letter to My Younger Self
items.text: Dear Jisoo, I know you are sitting at your desk tonight, convinced that one bad grade has ruined everything. I wish I could sit beside you and say what no one said to me. That test will soon be forgotten. What you will remember is how you reacted: whether you gave up, or whether you asked for help and tried again. You are not behind; you are simply learning at your own speed, and that is allowed. Be kind to yourself, the way you would be to a friend. Call your grandmother more often. And please, stop comparing your chapter one to everyone else's chapter ten. It gets lighter, I promise. With love, the Jisoo you will become.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the letter?
o: To comfort and encourage a discouraged student
To complain about unfair grading at school
To announce a plan for the writer's future career
To describe in detail how a test is organized
qs.why: 과거의 자신을 위로하고 격려하는 편지예요.

qs.q: Which word best describes the writer's tone?
o: Cold and critical
Humorous and careless
Suspicious and guarded
Gentle and reassuring
qs.why: 다정하고 안심시키는 어조예요.

qs.q: What does "stop comparing your chapter one to everyone else's chapter ten" mean?
o: Do not read books that are too long for your age.
Do not copy other students' answers during a test.
Do not judge your early progress against people who are much further along.
Do not skip the early chapters of your textbook.
qs.why: 남의 완성된 모습과 자기의 시작 단계를 비교하지 말라는 비유예요.

qs.q: Who is "the Jisoo you will become"?
o: A classmate who studies at the next desk and often shares notes with Jisoo
The writer, who is older than the person being addressed
A younger cousin who looks up to Jisoo
A teacher who graded Jisoo's last test
qs.why: 미래의 자신이 과거의 자신에게 쓴 편지라는 구조예요.

items.title: The Harbor at Dusk
items.text: By six o'clock the fog had swallowed the harbor. Boats appeared and disappeared like half-remembered thoughts, and the only sound was the slow groan of ropes against old wood. Nobody walked along the pier. The lamps, one by one, flickered on, each ringed by a pale, trembling halo that lit nothing but itself. Somewhere far away, a bell rang twice and then fell silent, as though it had thought better of it. Mara pulled her coat tighter and told herself that the shadow at the end of the dock was only a stack of crates. But the stack of crates, she noticed, had just moved. She held her breath and waited, unable to take a single step back.

qs.q: What is the dominant mood of the passage?
o: Eerie and suspenseful
Festive and lively
Humorous and light
Calm and cheerful
qs.why: 안개, 침묵, 움직이는 그림자가 으스스하고 긴장된 분위기를 만들어요.

qs.q: Which detail contributes most to the mood?
o: The ropes tied firmly to old wooden boats along the whole pier
The time of day being six o'clock
The coat that Mara pulls around herself
The silent pier and the flickering lamps in the fog
qs.why: 인적 없는 부두와 깜빡이는 등이 불안감을 줘요.

qs.q: What is suggested by "the stack of crates had just moved"?
o: The harbor workers are carrying goods to a ship.
A strong wave has pushed the crates along the pier.
Something unknown may be hiding at the end of the dock.
Mara has finally found the crates she was seeking.
qs.why: 움직이는 그림자는 정체 모를 존재를 암시해요.

qs.q: What does the phrase "as though it had thought better of it" imply about the bell?
o: It was too old and rusty to make any sound, so the noise came from somewhere else.
It stopped ringing suddenly, as if it had changed its mind.
It was broken by the heavy fog around it.
It rang louder because nobody was nearby.
qs.why: 종이 두 번 울리고 갑자기 멈춘 모습을 의인화한 표현이에요.

items.title: About My Order
items.text: Dear Customer Service, I am writing about order number 48213, which I placed three weeks ago for a winter coat. I was told it would arrive within five days. It did not, and when I called, I was twice informed that the package was "on its way." It has now been twenty-one days. I understand that delays occur, but I do not understand why no one has contacted me to explain. Frankly, I am disappointed, especially since the cold weather has already arrived. I would appreciate it if you could either deliver the coat by Friday or refund my payment in full. I trust that you will treat this matter with the urgency it deserves. Yours faithfully, Hana Park

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
o: To demand a solution to a delayed delivery
To thank the shop for fast service
To ask for advice on choosing a winter coat
To cancel membership of a shopping club
qs.why: 배송 지연에 대해 해결(배송 또는 환불)을 요구하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes the tone?
o: Rude and insulting
Joyful and relaxed
Confused and shy
Firm but polite
qs.why: 불만은 분명히 표현하되 "I would appreciate it" 등 예의를 지켜요.

qs.q: How long has the writer waited for the coat?
o: Five days
Three days
Twenty-one days
Two days
qs.why: 21일이 지났다고 직접 나와 있어요.

qs.q: What does the writer want if the coat is not delivered by Friday?
o: A free replacement of a different color
A full refund of the payment
A discount coupon for the next order
A written apology from the manager
qs.why: 배송이 안 되면 전액 환불을 요구했어요.

items.title: Day Twelve Without My Phone
items.text: Day twelve of my phone fast, and I have made some discoveries. First, my thumbs, deprived of scrolling, have started twitching on the bus like tiny, abandoned pets. Second, it turns out the sky does things. Clouds move! Nobody had warned me. Third, I have developed an embarrassing habit of reaching for my pocket whenever a conversation goes quiet, only to find lint and a single sad coin. My friends say I am "more present." I say I am more bored, but I am also noticing small things, like the way our bus driver hums the same four notes every morning. I will report back after day thirty, assuming I survive and still remember how to send a text message.

qs.q: Which word best describes the writer's tone?
o: Humorous and self-mocking
Bitter and angry toward the whole world
Solemn and respectful
Frightened and desperate
qs.why: 과장과 농담으로 자신을 놀리는 유머러스한 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say "Clouds move! Nobody had warned me"?
o: To warn readers about a coming storm
To explain a scientific fact about weather
To complain that nobody had told the news
To joke about how little attention was paid to the sky before
qs.why: 구름이 움직인다는 사실에 놀란 척하며 유머를 만들어요.

qs.q: What does the writer imply about the experience?
o: It has been a complete failure from the first day.
It has made the writer lose all of their friends and stop talking to them completely.
It is difficult, yet it is making the writer notice more things.
It has been so easy that it needs no effort.
qs.why: 지루하다고 하면서도 주변의 작은 것을 알아차린다고 했어요.

qs.q: What is the meaning of "deprived of" in the passage?
o: Fully satisfied with
Kept from having
Responsible for
Extremely proud of
qs.why: deprived of는 ~을 빼앗긴, ~을 못 가진이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Winter at the Night Market
items.text: When the first snow of December settled on the rooftops, the night market glowed like a lantern in a dark field. Stalls steamed with dumplings and sweet red-bean buns, and the cold air tasted of roasted chestnuts. An old man handed me a paper cup of hot barley tea and refused my coins, saying only, "Keep warm, young one." Children in puffy jackets chased one another between the tables, their laughter rising above the clatter of pots. I stood a while with the cup in both hands, feeling the heat spread slowly to my fingers, and thought that perhaps this was what people meant by the word "home": not a building, but a feeling of being looked after by strangers.

qs.q: What is the atmosphere of the market in this passage?
o: Warm and welcoming
Dangerous and dark
Lonely and silent
Rushed and angry
qs.why: 따뜻한 음식과 친절한 사람들로 포근한 분위기예요.

qs.q: Why does the old man refuse the narrator's coins?
o: He believes the coins are not real money.
He has already sold all the tea in his stall.
He is afraid the narrator will not come back.
He wants to show simple kindness to a visitor in the cold.
qs.why: "Keep warm"라는 말에서 순수한 친절을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does the narrator suggest "home" really means?
o: A building with a strong roof, many rooms, and a warm kitchen for the whole family
A place where one was born and has always lived
A sense of being cared for, even by people one does not know
A quiet room where nobody ever disturbs you
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 집이란 낯선 이에게도 돌봄을 받는 느낌이라고 말해요.

qs.q: The phrase "glowed like a lantern in a dark field" mainly shows that the market was
o: too small to be seen from afar
bright and inviting against the dark
closed because of the heavy snow
as quiet as an empty farm
qs.why: 어둠 속 등불 같다는 비유는 밝고 반가운 모습을 나타내요.

items.title: Should Students Wear Uniforms?
items.text: Schools across the country continue to argue about uniforms. Supporters say that a common outfit reduces pressure to follow expensive fashion, helps students feel part of one community, and saves families time each morning. Critics reply that uniforms limit self-expression and can be uncomfortable, especially in hot weather. A recent survey of one thousand students found that fifty-four percent preferred wearing uniforms, while forty-six percent opposed them. Interestingly, the opinions varied more by school than by age. Teachers in the study reported that discipline did not noticeably change, but several noted that fewer arguments about clothing took place. Researchers conclude that the effect of uniforms is real but modest, and that local conditions probably matter more than any general rule.

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone of the passage?
o: Objective
Emotional
Sarcastic
Boastful
qs.why: 양쪽 입장과 조사 결과를 치우침 없이 전달하는 객관적인 어조예요.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
o: To persuade readers to ban all school uniforms
To tell a story about a student who disliked his uniform
To advertise a company that produces school clothes
To present both sides of a debate along with survey data
qs.why: 찬반 의견과 설문 자료를 균형 있게 소개해요.

qs.q: Which statement is supported by the survey described?
o: Most students strongly opposed wearing uniforms.
Opinions depended mainly on the age and the grade level of the students.
Slightly more than half of the students preferred uniforms.
Teachers said that discipline improved greatly.
qs.why: 54퍼센트가 찬성이라고 했어요.

qs.q: What do the researchers conclude?
o: Uniforms completely solve problems of discipline.
Uniforms have a real but limited effect, depending on the school.
Uniforms have absolutely no effect on school life.
Uniforms should be the same in every school.
qs.why: 효과는 있지만 크지 않고 지역 조건이 더 중요하다고 결론 내렸어요.

items.title: After the Rain
items.text: The storm had passed in the night, and morning arrived washed and quiet. Water still dripped from the leaves, one slow drop at a time, and the garden smelled of wet earth and crushed mint. Ayaan sat on the porch step with a blanket over his knees, watching a snail cross the stone path as if it had all the time in the world. There was no hurry in anything: not the clouds drifting apart, not the sparrow bathing in a puddle, not his own breathing. His phone, face down on the boards, buzzed twice and was ignored. For the first time in weeks, he thought of nothing at all, and the nothing felt like a kind of wealth.

qs.q: What is the mood of the passage?
o: Serene
Anxious
Bitter
Chaotic
qs.why: 고요하고 평온한 분위기예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention the snail "as if it had all the time in the world"?
o: To show that the snail is injured and cannot move any farther across the path
To suggest that Ayaan is late for an appointment
To explain why the garden has become unhealthy
To stress the unhurried, relaxed pace of the morning
qs.why: 서두르지 않는 느린 흐름을 강조해요.

qs.q: What does "the nothing felt like a kind of wealth" mean?
o: He had found money hidden in the garden.
He regretted having nothing to do that day.
Having an empty, calm mind was something valuable to him.
He was sad because his garden was empty.
qs.why: 아무 생각 없는 평온함이 귀한 것으로 느껴졌다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does ignoring the buzzing phone suggest about Ayaan?
o: He is angry with the person calling him and wants to be left alone.
He wants to enjoy the peace without interruption.
He has lost the phone somewhere in the garden.
He is waiting for an urgent message.
qs.why: 전화를 무시하는 것은 평온을 방해받고 싶지 않다는 표시예요.

items.title: Grandfather's Watch
items.text: The watch had not worked for years, but Grandfather never stopped winding it. Every evening, after supper, he took it out of the drawer, turned the tiny crown a few times, and held it to his ear as if listening for a heartbeat. When I asked why, he only smiled. After he passed away last spring, my mother gave it to me. Yesterday, curious, I took it to a repair shop. The watchmaker opened the case and found a folded scrap of paper tucked inside, written in Grandfather's careful handwriting: "Time is only worth keeping when someone is waiting to share it." I carried the watch home in my palm, and for the first time since the funeral, I cried and smiled together.

qs.q: Which word best describes the mood of the ending?
o: Bittersweet
Cheerful
Threatening
Mysterious
qs.why: 슬픔과 따뜻함이 함께 있는 쓰고도 달콤한 분위기예요.

qs.q: Why did Grandfather keep winding the broken watch?
o: He hoped to sell it to a collector for a good price.
He wanted to hide it from the other family members.
He believed it would soon start to work by itself.
The ritual seems to have held a special personal meaning for him.
qs.why: 고장 난 시계를 매일 감는 행동은 개인적 의미가 있었음을 보여 줘요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the note found inside the watch?
o: Watches should be repaired as often as possible, however much it costs.
Old objects are worth more than new ones.
Time becomes valuable when it is shared with other people.
People should never waste their money on gifts.
qs.why: 쪽지는 시간을 누군가와 나눌 때 가치가 있다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What does "I cried and smiled together" suggest about the narrator?
o: The narrator found the watchmaker's joke very funny.
The narrator felt grief and warm affection at the same time.
The narrator was embarrassed to be seen in public.
The narrator felt nothing about the discovery.
qs.why: 슬픔과 애정이 동시에 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Warning: Thin Ice
items.text: Attention all visitors to Maple Lake. Although recent temperatures have dropped, the ice on the lake is NOT safe. Last week, two skaters broke through near the eastern shore and had to be rescued by park staff. Ice that looks solid may be only a few centimeters thick, and it can change dramatically within hours. Please do not walk, skate, or let pets run on the surface under any circumstances. Children must remain on the paths at all times. The park will announce when the ice has been tested and approved, and we ask that you do not attempt to judge its safety yourself. A moment of carelessness can have serious consequences. Thank you for helping us keep everyone safe.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this announcement?
o: To warn visitors against going onto the frozen lake
To invite visitors to a skating competition on the frozen lake this weekend
To report the winner of a rescue award
To describe the history of Maple Lake
qs.why: 얼음 위에 올라가지 말라는 경고문이에요.

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone?
o: Playful and teasing
Gloomy and hopeless
Admiring and grateful
Serious and cautionary
qs.why: 위험을 강조하며 조심시키는 진지한 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention the two skaters?
o: To praise the skaters for their courage in testing the ice by themselves
To announce that the lake is now open to skaters
To show that the danger is real and has already caused trouble
To explain how to take part in a rescue
qs.why: 실제 사고 사례를 들어 위험이 현실임을 보여 줘요.

qs.q: What does the park ask visitors NOT to do?
o: Visit the lake during the coming weekend
Decide for themselves whether the ice is safe
Take photographs of the eastern shore
Report problems to the park staff
qs.why: 스스로 안전을 판단하지 말라고 했어요.

items.title: The Meeting About Meetings
items.text: At nine o'clock sharp, forty employees gathered in the conference room to discuss the company's most urgent problem: too many meetings. A cheerful manager opened with a slide titled "Reducing Meetings Through Meetings." Everyone nodded gravely. Over the next two hours, we agreed that a committee should be formed to study the issue, that the committee would meet weekly, and that a follow-up meeting would be scheduled to review the committee's progress. Brilliant, really. By eleven, we had solved nothing, but I must admit the coffee was excellent. As we filed out, a colleague whispered, "Same time next week?" and I laughed so hard that I had to pretend I was coughing.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward the meeting?
o: Ironic and amused
Respectful and grateful
Furious and aggressive
Frightened and uncertain
qs.why: 회의를 줄이기 위해 회의를 연다는 모순을 비꼬며 즐기는 어조예요.

qs.q: What does "Brilliant, really" most likely mean here?
o: The plan was truly the cleverest idea ever suggested, and the writer sincerely admires it.
The writer admires the manager's speaking skills.
The meeting solved the problem within two hours.
The plan was actually ridiculous, but the writer is saying the opposite.
qs.why: 반어법으로, 실제로는 한심한 결정을 비꼬는 말이에요.

qs.q: Why is the title "Reducing Meetings Through Meetings" humorous?
o: It uses a very long and difficult word.
It was printed in a color that no one could read.
It contains a contradiction between the goal and the method.
It describes a meeting that had already ended.
qs.why: 회의를 줄이려고 회의를 한다는 모순 때문에 우스워요.

qs.q: What happened by eleven o'clock?
o: The group had finally solved the problem and gone home to celebrate the result.
The group had made decisions but had not truly solved the problem.
The group was still waiting for the manager to arrive.
The group had decided to cancel all future meetings.
qs.why: 위원회와 후속 회의만 정했을 뿐 문제는 해결되지 않았어요.

items.title: Why I Am Applying
items.text: Dear Scholarship Committee, My name is Minjun Seo, and I am a senior at Haneul High School. I am writing to apply for the Future Engineers Scholarship. Since I repaired my neighbor's broken radio at the age of ten, I have wanted to understand how things work and, one day, to design machines that help people. My family cannot easily afford university fees, so this scholarship would make an enormous difference. I have spent the past two years leading our school's robotics club, where we built a sensor that warns elderly residents about floor water. I would be honored to continue learning in your program and to repay your trust with hard work. Thank you for considering my application.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the letter?
o: To apply for financial support for university study
To complain about the rules of a robotics club
To thank a neighbor for repairing a radio
To ask the school to buy new equipment
qs.why: 장학금 신청서예요.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes the writer's tone?
o: Careless and a little boastful
Angry and demanding
Mocking and playful
Sincere and respectful
qs.why: 정중하고 진심 어린 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention repairing the radio?
o: To prove that his neighbor is wealthy
To explain why his family needs more money
To show that his interest in machines began early
To suggest that he dislikes his school
qs.why: 어릴 때부터 기계에 관심이 있었음을 보여 주려는 거예요.

qs.q: Which of the following is true about Minjun?
o: He has already finished university and now works as an engineer.
He has led a robotics club for two years.
He studies at a school overseas.
He has never built anything himself.
qs.why: 지난 2년간 로봇 동아리를 이끌었다고 했어요.

items.title: Robot Teachers?
items.text: A new school in the north has announced that robots will teach mathematics from next year, and the headline writers are thrilled. I am less certain. Of course, a machine never tires, never forgets a formula, and never loses its temper. But can it notice the student at the back who has stopped asking questions, or sense that a joke is needed to break an afternoon silence? The company promises "personalized learning," a phrase that, to me, sounds suspiciously like a product label. Technology can certainly assist teachers, and I welcome that. Yet replacing them is a different matter, and we should not mistake efficiency for education simply because the numbers on a screen look impressive.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward robot teachers?
o: Doubtful
Enthusiastic
Indifferent
Fearful
qs.why: 수용은 하되 의심 많은 회의적 태도예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer call "personalized learning" a product label?
o: The writer has bought a product with that name.
The writer believes the phrase is difficult to pronounce.
The writer thinks the phrase appears on school uniforms.
The writer suspects it is a sales slogan rather than a real promise.
qs.why: 광고 문구처럼 들린다며 의심을 나타내요.

qs.q: Which statement would the writer most likely agree with?
o: Teachers should be replaced by machines as soon as possible, because machines never tire.
Technology has no place in modern classrooms.
Technology is useful when it supports teachers rather than replaces them.
Students learn best when no one is watching them.
qs.why: 기술은 교사를 돕는 것은 환영하지만 대체는 반대해요.

qs.q: What does the writer mean by "mistake efficiency for education"?
o: Believing education should be free of charge
Treating fast results as proof that real learning is happening
Assuming robots are cheaper than textbooks
Confusing school lessons with sports training
qs.why: 효율을 교육 자체로 착각하지 말라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Moving Day
items.text: The truck was parked outside, half-loaded, when Eun-ji found herself standing alone in her empty bedroom. The walls still showed pale squares where her posters had hung for six years. She knew the new city had a bigger school, a famous art program, and a room with a balcony. She also knew that nobody there would know her name. Her chest felt tight and light at once, like a balloon held by a very thin string. Downstairs, her father shouted that it was time to go. She ran her hand along the doorframe, where her height had been marked every birthday, and whispered a quiet goodbye. Then, taking a breath, she picked up her bag and walked toward whatever was next.

qs.q: How does Eun-ji feel in the passage?
o: Sad about leaving yet hopeful about the future
Relieved to be rid of the old house and the old neighbors
Furious at her father for the decision
Completely unconcerned about the move
qs.why: 아쉬움과 기대가 섞인 복합적 감정이에요.

qs.q: What does "tight and light at once" describe?
o: The physical weight of her heavy bag
A medical problem that she is suffering from
The size of her new bedroom
Mixed feelings of worry and excitement
qs.why: 상반된 감정이 동시에 있음을 나타내요.

qs.q: What do the pale squares on the walls suggest?
o: Her family could not afford to paint the walls.
The posters had been removed by mistake.
She had lived in the room for a long time.
She dislikes the color of the walls.
qs.why: 6년간 포스터가 붙어 있던 흔적이에요.

qs.q: Why does she touch the doorframe?
o: She wants to check whether it needs repairs.
It holds memories of her growing up.
She is hoping the new owner will not notice it.
She is angry and wants to damage it.
qs.why: 키를 표시해 둔 문틀에서 추억을 느끼는 거예요.

items.title: A Night in the Desert
items.text: When the sun slid behind the dunes, the desert did not go dark; it went quiet. One by one, the stars appeared, first a handful, then hundreds, then so many that the sky seemed to be breathing. Our guide put out the fire and asked us to lie flat on the sand. For a long time nobody spoke. The Milky Way stretched overhead like spilled milk, and a shooting star drew a thin white line and vanished before I could even make a wish. I felt very small, but strangely it was not a frightening feeling. It was the feeling of belonging to something far larger than my worries, and the sand beneath me still held the warmth of the day.

qs.q: Which word best describes the narrator's feeling?
o: Awe
Boredom
Envy
Disgust
qs.why: 광활한 별 하늘 앞에서 느끼는 경외감이에요.

qs.q: Why does the narrator say feeling small was "not a frightening feeling"?
o: The narrator was no longer afraid of the dark desert.
The narrator was accompanied by an experienced guide.
The narrator had seen the same stars many times.
It brought a comforting sense of being part of something vast.
qs.why: 작음이 두려움이 아니라 위안과 소속감으로 느껴졌다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why did the guide put out the fire?
o: Because the sand was becoming too hot
Because the group was ready to go to sleep
So the stars could be seen more clearly
Because the wind was blowing out the flames
qs.why: 불을 끄면 별이 더 잘 보이기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does "the sky seemed to be breathing" suggest?
o: The wind was blowing hard across the dunes and shaking the whole sky.
The stars looked alive as they appeared in growing numbers.
The sky was filled with dark rain clouds.
The group could hear the breath of animals.
qs.why: 별이 점점 많아지는 모습을 살아 있는 것처럼 표현했어요.

items.title: Thank You, Ms. Alvarez
items.text: Subject: Thank you. Dear Ms. Alvarez, I hope you are well. I wanted to write before the term ends to say how much your English classes have meant to me. When I arrived in September, I was too shy to speak, and I used to sit silently at the back, hoping nobody would call on me. You never forced me. Instead, you waited, smiled, and let me answer in my own time. Last week, I gave a presentation to the whole class without shaking, and I realized I was enjoying it. I owe that confidence to you. I will remember your patience for the rest of my life. With sincere thanks, Yuna Kim

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
o: To express thanks for a teacher's support
To ask for a higher grade on an assignment
To report a problem with the English class
To invite the teacher to a school event
qs.why: 감사 이메일이에요.

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone?
o: Sarcastic
Anxious
Impatient
Grateful
qs.why: 진심 어린 감사를 전하는 어조예요.

qs.q: How did Yuna feel in the class at the beginning?
o: Eager to give a presentation
Angry about the choice of seats
Too shy to speak in front of others
Bored by the quiet lessons
qs.why: 9월에는 수줍어서 말을 못 했다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the writer imply about Ms. Alvarez's teaching style?
o: She was strict and called on students at random.
She was patient and did not pressure students.
She seldom spoke to students after class.
She wanted students to speak only in groups.
qs.why: 강요하지 않고 기다려 주었다는 점에서 인내심 있는 교사예요.

items.title: Stories in Stone
items.text: Welcome to the Hall of Early Writing. Before you stands the oldest object in our collection: a clay tablet, about the size of a child's hand, pressed with wedge-shaped marks more than four thousand years ago. Experts believe it records a delivery of barley, which means that some of the first words ever written were not poems or prayers, but receipts. This may disappoint those who imagine ancient writers pouring out grand ideas, yet it reminds us that writing began as a practical tool for solving everyday problems. Please look closely at the tiny, careful lines, and try to imagine the person who made them. We invite you to move on to the next case, where you will see how these simple marks gradually became letters.

qs.q: What is the tone of the passage?
o: Informative with a touch of curiosity
Angry and critical of everything on display
Mournful and regretful
Fearful and suspicious
qs.why: 정보를 전달하며 호기심을 자극하는 어조예요.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
o: To argue that poems are more important than receipts
To warn visitors to stay away from the tablet
To advertise tickets for a museum shop
To introduce an exhibit and explain what it shows
qs.why: 전시물을 소개하고 설명하는 안내문이에요.

qs.q: What does the tablet most likely record?
o: A poem about the harvest
A prayer for good weather
A delivery of barley
A list of the names of kings
qs.why: 보리 배달 기록이라고 설명해요.

qs.q: What does the writer mean by "this may disappoint those who imagine ancient writers pouring out grand ideas"?
o: Early writers were not able to read their own words.
Early writing was probably more ordinary than people expect.
Ancient poems have never been discovered.
The museum has lost its most important collection.
qs.why: 초기 글쓰기가 거창하지 않고 실용적이었다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: What He Promised
items.text: Tomas had promised to come on Saturday. I know, because I wrote it on the calendar in red and told the whole class. By ten o'clock, I had set the table. By noon, I had stopped looking at the door. At two, my mother said gently that he was probably busy, and I said, "It doesn't matter," in the voice I use when it matters most. In the evening, a short message appeared on my phone: "Sorry, something came up." That was all. No reason, no new date. I put the phone face down and stared at the cold dinner I had cooked myself. People say that words are cheap, but I have learned that some of them cost a great deal when they are broken.

qs.q: What is the narrator's attitude at the end?
o: Hurt and disappointed
Delighted and relieved
Curious and playful
Proud and confident
qs.why: 약속을 어긴 데 대한 상처와 실망이에요.

qs.q: What does "It doesn't matter" actually show?
o: The narrator had never really wanted Tomas to visit the house at all.
The narrator was busy with something else.
The narrator agrees with the mother's opinion.
The narrator is pretending not to care while feeling upset.
qs.why: "when it matters most"라고 해서 속마음은 반대임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the narrator say "some of them cost a great deal when they are broken"?
o: Words are sold at a high price in shops.
Messages on phones are expensive to send.
Broken promises can cause deep emotional pain.
Dinner had been cooked from costly ingredients.
qs.why: 어긴 약속의 정서적 대가가 크다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the sequence of times (ten, noon, two) mainly show?
o: How long it takes to cook a dinner
How the narrator's hope slowly faded
How busy the narrator's day was
How quickly the afternoon passed
qs.why: 시간이 흐르며 기대가 줄어드는 과정을 보여 줘요.

items.title: Lantern Night
items.text: By the time the sun set, the entire riverbank had turned into a sea of color. Hundreds of paper lanterns bobbed in the hands of children, glowing red, gold, and green, while drummers on a wooden stage pounded out a rhythm that I felt in my ribs. Street vendors shouted prices over the music, and the smell of grilled corn drifted through the crowd. My little cousin, perched on his father's shoulders, clapped so hard that his lantern nearly flew away. When the first firework burst above the water, a single gasp ran through everyone, followed by a roar of joy. I looked around at the glowing faces and realized I had been grinning for so long that my cheeks hurt.

qs.q: What is the mood of the scene?
o: Festive and joyful
Quiet and lonely
Tense and dangerous
Sad and serious
qs.why: 축제의 흥겹고 즐거운 분위기예요.

qs.q: What is suggested by "my cheeks hurt"?
o: The narrator had been hit by a lantern.
The narrator was feeling the cold wind blowing along the riverbank.
The narrator was unhappy with the loud noise.
The narrator had been smiling for a very long time.
qs.why: 오래 웃어서 볼이 아프다는 뜻으로 즐거움을 강조해요.

qs.q: What happened when the first firework burst?
o: The crowd quickly left the riverbank.
The drummers stopped playing at once.
The crowd gasped and then cheered.
The vendors began to lower their prices.
qs.why: 숨을 들이쉰 뒤 환호성이 터졌다고 해요.

qs.q: Which detail appeals to the sense of smell?
o: The drums pounding on the wooden stage
The grilled corn drifting through the crowd
The red, gold, and green lanterns
The vendors shouting prices
qs.why: 옥수수 굽는 냄새가 후각 묘사예요.

items.title: The Reef Report
items.text: According to a recent survey, nearly a third of the coral in the northern part of the reef has turned white in the past two years. Scientists explain that warmer water forces corals to expel the tiny algae that give them color and food. If the water cools quickly, corals can recover; if not, they starve. The survey recorded a rise in average sea temperature of 1.2 degrees since 2000. Researchers caution that the figures, though serious, do not mean the reef is beyond saving. Reducing local pollution and limiting fishing in key areas have helped some sections regrow. The team recommends continued monitoring and urges governments to act without delay, noting that every additional half degree of warming makes recovery harder.

qs.q: What is the tone of the report?
o: Concerned yet measured
Humorous and relaxed
Panicked and completely hopeless
Cheerful and boastful
qs.why: 심각하지만 감정적이지 않고 절제된 어조예요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: The reef has been completely destroyed and cannot recover.
Fishing is the only cause of coral loss.
Coral prefers warmer water to cooler water.
Warming seas are damaging the reef, but action can still help.
qs.why: 피해가 크지만 대응으로 회복할 수 있다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What happens to corals when they expel their algae?
o: They grow faster in the warm water.
They change into a different kind of animal.
They lose color and food, and may starve.
They move to cooler parts of the ocean.
qs.why: 조류를 내보내면 색과 영양분을 잃고 굶을 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why do the researchers say the figures "do not mean the reef is beyond saving"?
o: The survey was not carried out carefully enough to be trusted.
Some areas have regrown after local protection measures.
The sea temperature has begun to fall again.
Governments have already solved the problem.
qs.why: 오염 감소와 어업 제한으로 일부 구역이 회복되었어요.

items.title: The Night Nurse
items.text: At three in the morning, when most of the city is asleep, Nurse Okafor is making her fourth round of the ward. She moves quietly, adjusting a pillow here, checking a monitor there, and pausing beside a frightened patient to murmur a few words that no medicine could replace. She has not sat down since midnight. Her feet ache, but she would never mention it. When a young man in bed six asks if he will be all right, she holds his hand and answers, "You are not alone tonight." I watched her do this and felt ashamed of how often I complain about small things. People like her rarely appear in the news, yet they hold the whole building together.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward Nurse Okafor?
o: Deep admiration
Mild irritation
Complete indifference
Quiet suspicion
qs.why: 헌신적인 모습에 대한 존경이에요.

qs.q: Why did the writer feel ashamed?
o: The writer had disturbed the patients during the night.
The writer had not been invited to work in the ward.
The writer had forgotten the nurse's name.
The writer realized how trivial their own complaints were by comparison.
qs.why: 간호사의 헌신과 비교해 자신의 불평이 사소하게 느껴졌어요.

qs.q: What does "hold the whole building together" mean here?
o: They repair the walls and floors of the hospital whenever something breaks.
They manage all of the hospital's money.
Such workers keep the hospital running through their steady effort.
They prevent patients from leaving the ward.
qs.why: 눈에 띄지 않아도 병원을 유지하는 핵심이라는 비유예요.

qs.q: What is the tone of Nurse Okafor's words to the patient?
o: Impatient
Comforting
Formal
Playful
qs.why: 손을 잡고 안심시키는 말이에요.

items.title: Missing: Biscuit
items.text: MISSING: Our beloved dog Biscuit disappeared from Willow Park on Tuesday evening. He is a small brown terrier with a white patch on his chest and one ear that never stands up. He is gentle, a little shy, and responds to the sound of a squeaky toy. Biscuit has a heart condition and needs his medicine twice a day, so every hour counts. Please check your sheds, garages, and gardens. If you see him, do not chase him; speak softly and call us right away. We will give a reward, but, honestly, we only want him home. My daughter has barely slept since Tuesday, and our house feels terribly empty without him. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the flyer?
o: To ask the public for help finding a lost pet
To advertise a dog food brand sold in the local park shop
To sell a puppy to a new owner
To announce a park event
qs.why: 실종된 반려견을 찾기 위한 호소문이에요.

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone?
o: Playful and joking
Cold and businesslike
Furious and blaming
Desperate yet hopeful
qs.why: 절박하지만 희망을 놓지 않는 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say "every hour counts"?
o: The reward becomes smaller as time passes.
The park closes soon in the evening.
The dog needs regular medicine for a health problem.
The daughter must leave for school soon.
qs.why: 심장 질환으로 약이 필요하기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What should people do if they see Biscuit?
o: Chase him until he stops running
Speak softly and contact the family
Take him to the park immediately
Wait for him to come back by himself
qs.why: 쫓지 말고 부드럽게 말하며 연락하라고 했어요.

items.title: The Trip That Wasn't
items.text: We had packed our bags on Wednesday. We had bought the tickets two months earlier, checked the weather twice, and even practiced a few phrases in the local language. Then, on Thursday morning, the airline sent a brief message: all flights canceled until further notice. I remember reading it twice, then putting my phone down and making breakfast, as if nothing unusual had happened. My sister kicked a suitcase and said a word she is not allowed to say. I only shrugged. There was no one to blame, no use in shouting, and no way to turn back time. We unpacked slowly that afternoon, folding each shirt as if it were something fragile, and quietly decided to try again next year.

qs.q: How does the narrator react to the news?
o: With quiet acceptance
With loud anger at the airline
With wild excitement
With sudden fear
qs.why: 화내지 않고 조용히 받아들여요.

qs.q: What is the tone of the last sentence?
o: Triumphant
Sarcastic
Playful
Resigned
qs.why: 체념했지만 내년을 기약하는 담담한 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention the sister kicking the suitcase?
o: To show that the suitcase was broken before
To explain that she disliked the destination
To show how differently the two of them reacted
To suggest that she caused the cancellation
qs.why: 언니/여동생이 화를 겉으로 드러낸 것과 화자의 담담한 반응이 서로 다르다는 것을 보여 주려는 거예요.

qs.q: What does "folding each shirt as if it were something fragile" suggest?
o: The shirts were made of very thin glass.
The narrator felt gently sad while unpacking.
The narrator was in a rush to finish unpacking.
The narrator wanted to sell the shirts.
qs.why: 조심스럽게 옷을 개는 행동에서 차분한 아쉬움을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Is a Four-Day Week the Answer?
items.text: Last year, a mid-sized software company moved to a four-day work week without reducing pay, and the results surprised even its own managers. Productivity stayed level, sick days dropped by a quarter, and employees reported sleeping better. Supporters argue that rested workers make fewer mistakes and stay longer with a company. Critics counter that the experiment is too small to prove anything, and that factory or hospital jobs cannot easily be compressed. Both points deserve respect. Yet it is hard to ignore the central lesson: the old assumption that more hours always mean more output has never been fully tested. Before we dismiss the idea as unrealistic, we should at least run more careful trials in a wider range of workplaces.

qs.q: What is the writer's position?
o: Open to the idea but in favor of more testing
Totally against shorter work weeks of any kind
Certain that all firms should adopt the plan
Uninterested in the results of the trial
qs.why: 찬반 양측을 인정하며 더 많은 시험을 주장해요.

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone?
o: Mocking
Panicked
Sentimental
Balanced yet persuasive
qs.why: 균형을 유지하면서도 시도를 권하는 어조예요.

qs.q: According to the critics, what is a weakness of the experiment?
o: It reduced the pay of workers by about a quarter.
It increased the number of sick days.
It was too limited to show general results.
It lasted for several decades.
qs.why: 표본이 작아서 증명하기 어렵다고 비판해요.

qs.q: What does the writer mean by "has never been fully tested"?
o: Researchers have proved that it is false.
People have assumed it without carefully checking whether it is true.
The idea has been tested only in factories.
Employees refuse to take part in any test.
qs.why: 충분히 검증되지 않은 채 당연시되어 왔다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Stage Fright
items.text: The curtain was still down, but I could hear the audience: hundreds of coughs, creaking seats, and whispered conversations. My script had turned into a blur of black marks, and my mouth felt as dry as paper. "Just breathe," whispered Hyeri from behind a painted tree. I nodded, though I did not believe her. Then the lights rose, and the first line of the play simply came out of me, as if someone else were speaking through my mouth. Halfway through the opening scene, a woman in the front row laughed at exactly the right moment, and something in my chest loosened. By the time the final bow arrived, I could hardly remember being afraid at all.

qs.q: How does the narrator's feeling change?
o: From fear to relief and confidence
From great joy to deep boredom and then to sleep
From anger to sadness
From calm to panic
qs.why: 무대 전의 두려움이 관객 반응 후 안도와 자신감으로 바뀌어요.

qs.q: What caused the narrator's tension to loosen?
o: Hyeri took over the narrator's lines.
The curtain was lifted earlier than planned.
The script was changed at the last minute.
A member of the audience laughed at the right moment.
qs.why: 관객의 웃음이 긴장을 풀어 줬어요.

qs.q: What does "my mouth felt as dry as paper" show?
o: The narrator was thirsty after a long walk.
The narrator was bored by the play.
The narrator was extremely nervous.
The narrator was ill with a cold.
qs.why: 긴장해서 입이 마른 상태를 비유한 표현이에요.

qs.q: What does "I nodded, though I did not believe her" suggest about the narrator?
o: The narrator was too anxious to be calmed by the advice.
The narrator was angry that Hyeri had interrupted the rehearsal.
The narrator had decided to leave the stage before the play began.
The narrator thought Hyeri's advice was clearly harmful.
qs.why: 고개는 끄덕였지만 믿지 못했다는 것은 조언만으로 불안이 가라앉지 않았다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: I Owe You an Apology
items.text: Dear Soyeon, I have started this letter four times and thrown away each attempt, because every sentence sounded like an excuse. So let me be plain: what I said at your birthday party was cruel, and I am sorry. I was tired and embarrassed about my own mistakes, and I took it out on you in front of everyone. That is no justification. I have thought about your face every day since, and I cannot stop wishing I had stayed silent. You do not need to forgive me right now. I only wanted you to know that I understand how much I hurt you, and that our friendship matters far more to me than my pride ever did. Whenever you are ready, I will be here.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the letter?
o: To apologize sincerely for hurtful words
To invite Soyeon to another party
To blame Soyeon for a misunderstanding
To announce the end of a friendship
qs.why: 사과 편지예요.

qs.q: Which word best describes the writer's tone?
o: Defensive and unwilling to listen
Cheerful
Casual
Remorseful
qs.why: 깊이 뉘우치는 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say "every sentence sounded like an excuse"?
o: The writer is not able to write in the correct language.
The writer has lost the paper for the letter.
The writer wants to apologize without making excuses.
The writer believes the apology is unnecessary.
qs.why: 변명처럼 들릴까 봐 여러 번 다시 썼다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer value more than pride?
o: The success of the party
The friendship with Soyeon
The quality of the letter
The opinion of other guests
qs.why: 우정이 자존심보다 더 중요하다고 했어요.

items.title: Meet the AquaMate
items.text: Are you tired of forgetting to drink water? Meet the AquaMate, the only bottle that thinks for you! Its built-in sensor tracks every sip and gently glows when it is time to refill. Made from lightweight steel, it keeps drinks icy for twenty-four hours, and its sleek design fits in any bag. Thousands of happy customers say they feel sharper, calmer, and more energetic within just one week. Order today and receive a free carrying strap, but hurry: this special offer ends on Sunday! Do not let another dehydrated afternoon ruin your day. With the AquaMate in your hand, you are not just drinking water; you are drinking in a brighter future. Your best self is only a sip away.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this text?
o: To persuade readers to buy a product
To teach readers how a sensor is built
To report a scientific study of hydration
To warn readers about dangerous bottles
qs.why: 상품을 구매하게 하려는 광고예요.

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone?
o: Objective and cautious
Gloomy and doubtful
Formal and reserved
Enthusiastic and exaggerated
qs.why: 과장된 표현과 열정이 광고의 특징이에요.

qs.q: Which phrase is most likely an exaggeration?
o: "Made from lightweight steel"
"Keeps drinks icy for twenty-four hours"
"You are drinking in a brighter future"
"Receive a free carrying strap"
qs.why: 물병이 미래를 밝게 한다는 말은 과장이에요.

qs.q: Why does the advertisement say "hurry"?
o: To warn that the bottle is breaking and should be replaced
To create a sense of urgency to buy soon
To explain how to refill the bottle
To remind buyers to return the strap
qs.why: 일요일에 끝나는 행사를 강조해 서두르게 해요.

items.title: The Last Day of the Old Library
items.text: On the final Friday, the old town library opened its doors for the last time. Sunlight lay in long yellow stripes across the reading tables, and the smell of paper and dust seemed stronger than ever. Mr. Han, the librarian for thirty-one years, moved slowly between the shelves, straightening books that were already straight. A few old regulars sat in their usual seats, not reading, just sitting. When the clock struck five, no one stood up. A girl at the desk quietly asked if she could keep her library card as a souvenir, and Mr. Han, whose voice had never once trembled in three decades, simply nodded and looked away. The new building would be larger and brighter, but everyone knew it would be different.

qs.q: What is the mood of the passage?
o: Melancholy
Triumphant
Furious
Humorous
qs.why: 마지막 날의 쓸쓸하고 애잔한 분위기예요.

qs.q: Why did no one stand up when the clock struck five?
o: They were waiting for a new librarian to arrive that evening.
They did not hear the clock strike over the street noise.
They wanted to start reading new books before closing time.
They were reluctant to say goodbye to a place they loved.
qs.why: 떠나기 싫은 마음을 나타내요.

qs.q: What does Mr. Han's reaction to the girl's request suggest?
o: He was angry at the girl's request.
He had not understood her question.
He was too moved to speak.
He was bored with the end of his job.
qs.why: 목소리가 떨린 적이 없던 그가 고개만 끄덕이고 시선을 돌린 것은 감정이 북받쳤기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What is implied by "it would be different"?
o: The new library would have fewer books.
The new building could not replace the feeling of the old one.
The new library would be built in a different city far from the old one.
The librarian would no longer be needed.
qs.why: 새 건물이 크고 밝아도 옛 도서관의 정서를 대신할 수는 없다는 암시예요.

items.title: A Saturday of Giving
items.text: At eight in the morning, forty of us in matching green shirts gathered at the riverbank with gloves, bags, and a vague sense of dread. By noon, that dread had turned into something else entirely. We had filled ninety bags of trash, found a bicycle wheel and a lost shoe, and discovered that picking up litter is far more fun when everyone is racing and joking. An elderly man walking his dog stopped to thank us, saying he had waited years to see the river clean. I felt a surge of pride that I could not quite explain. As we sat on the grass sharing sandwiches, one volunteer said, "Imagine what we could do every month." Nobody laughed, because everyone was already imagining it.

qs.q: What is the overall mood at the end of the passage?
o: Uplifting and hopeful
Gloomy and tired
Tense and suspicious
Bored and distant
qs.why: 보람과 희망으로 가득한 분위기예요.

qs.q: How did the volunteers' feeling change during the morning?
o: From joy to disappointment and then anger
From boredom to anger
From confidence to fear
From reluctance to enjoyment and pride
qs.why: 처음의 막연한 걱정이 즐거움과 자부심으로 바뀌었어요.

qs.q: Why did nobody laugh at the volunteer's remark?
o: Everyone thought the remark was rude.
Everyone was too tired to hear the remark.
Everyone took the idea seriously and liked it.
Everyone had left before it was said.
qs.why: 모두 이미 그 가능성을 상상하고 있었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What did the elderly man say?
o: He wanted to join the volunteers next month and bring his dog along.
He had waited many years for the river to be clean.
He was upset about the noise of the group.
He lost his dog near the riverbank.
qs.why: 수년간 깨끗한 강을 기다렸다고 했어요.

items.title: One Chapter Away
items.text: The clock on my desk says two thirty, and my eyelids feel like sandbags. Tomorrow's exam covers six units, and I have fully understood only four. The house is silent except for the refrigerator and the occasional creak of the stairs. I could stop now; no one would blame me. But I keep thinking of the promise I made to my grandmother, who sold vegetables for forty years so that I could sit at this very desk. So I pour another cup of cold barley tea, rub my eyes, and open the textbook to page ninety. It is not heroic, and no one is watching. It is simply the next page, and then the one after that, and I intend to read them all.

qs.q: Which word best describes the narrator's attitude?
o: Determined
Careless
Resentful
Cheerful
qs.why: 지쳤지만 끝까지 해내겠다는 의지가 드러나요.

qs.q: Why does the narrator continue studying?
o: The narrator's parents are watching from behind.
The exam was moved to an earlier date by the school without notice.
The narrator wants to win a prize tonight.
A promise to the grandmother gives the narrator motivation.
qs.why: 할머니와의 약속이 동기가 돼요.

qs.q: What does "It is not heroic, and no one is watching" suggest?
o: The narrator is performing for a large and admiring audience.
The narrator regrets studying so seriously this late at night.
The narrator is working steadily without praise or attention.
The narrator is ashamed of the grades from the last exam.
qs.why: 누가 보지 않아도 묵묵히 해 나간다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the mood created by the silent house and the late hour?
o: Noisy and festive
Quiet and weary
Dangerous and tense
Silly and relaxed
qs.why: 고요하고 지친 분위기예요.

items.title: A Farewell From the Principal
items.text: Good afternoon, graduates, parents, and the few teachers who have not yet escaped. Four years ago, you arrived looking terrified, and I pretended to look calm; we were both fooling ourselves. Since then, you have survived late buses, impossible exams, and my speeches, which is perhaps the greater achievement. Today, I will not promise that life will be easy. It will not. But I have watched you comfort a friend, lead a rescue of a stray cat, and build a garden on a dull rooftop, and I am confident that you will manage. Go forward bravely, and remember: you are always welcome here, preferably when I am not giving another speech. Congratulations, and thank you for letting me be part of your story.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes the tone of the speech?
o: Warm and lightly humorous
Strict, cold, and unforgiving
Sad and apologetic
Cold and distant
qs.why: 따뜻하고 가벼운 유머가 섞인 어조예요.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the speech?
o: To criticize students for their poor behavior
To announce changes in school rules
To advertise next year's courses
To send graduates off with encouragement and thanks
qs.why: 졸업생에게 격려와 감사를 전하는 연설이에요.

qs.q: Why does the principal mention "my speeches"?
o: To warn students about an unusually long speech
To introduce the next speaker on the program
To make a joke at the speaker's own expense
To blame the teachers for the delay today
qs.why: 자기 연설을 농담거리로 삼아 분위기를 풀어요.

qs.q: What does the principal believe about the graduates' future?
o: They will find life easy and carefree.
They will cope well with its challenges.
They will forget their school immediately.
They will have no need of further help.
qs.why: 삶이 쉽지 않지만 잘 해낼 것이라 믿어요.

items.title: A Film Review
items.text: I wanted to like "The Silver Hour," I really did. The posters promised a bold, original adventure, and the cast is excellent. Unfortunately, the film spends nearly two and a half hours proving that talented people can be wasted on a hopeless script. The hero explains his feelings in speeches so long that I had time to count the ceiling tiles, and the villain's plan makes sense only if every character in the film is blind. The final twist, which the director clearly considers shocking, was guessed by the audience in the first twenty minutes. There are two or three beautiful shots of the sea, and those, sadly, are the film's only memorable moments. Bring a book. You will have plenty of time to read it.

qs.q: What is the reviewer's overall opinion of the film?
o: Largely negative, with only a few praised details
Enthusiastic about every part of it
Neutral, without any clear opinion
Positive about the story but negative about the actors
qs.why: 대부분 부정적이고 바다 장면만 칭찬해요.

qs.q: What is the tone of the final sentences, "Bring a book. You will have plenty of time to read it"?
o: Admiring
Fearful
Neutral
Sarcastic
qs.why: 영화가 지루하다는 것을 빈정대는 말이에요.

qs.q: Which of the following does the reviewer praise?
o: The long speeches of the hero
The surprising final twist
The cast and a few shots of the sea
The clever plan of the villain
qs.why: 배우와 바다 장면을 칭찬했어요.

qs.q: Why does the reviewer say the villain's plan makes sense "only if every character in the film is blind"?
o: The villain is actually a character who cannot see.
The plan is so obvious that the characters should have noticed it.
The film is set in a place without any light, so everyone is in the dark.
The characters wear dark glasses in every scene.
qs.why: 계획이 너무 허술해서 모두가 눈이 먼 것처럼 보이지 않는 한 말이 안 된다는 과장이에요.

items.title: A Very Quiet Dinner
items.text:
Jin: So, how was the test?
Dad: I asked you a question. How was it?
Jin: Fine.
Dad: Fine. That is your answer? I got a call from your teacher this afternoon.
Jin: Then you already know how it went.
Dad: I would rather hear it from you. I am not angry, Jin. I am worried.
Jin: Everyone says that, but you always sound angry.
Dad: Maybe I do. I am sorry. Let me try again. Tell me what happened, and I will listen until you are finished.
Jin: I froze. I knew the answers, but my mind went white. I did not want to disappoint you.
Dad: Thank you for telling me. You could never disappoint me by being human.
Jin: Even if I fail?
Dad: Especially then. Now, eat before the soup gets cold.

qs.q: How does the father's attitude change during the conversation?
o: From stern to gentle and understanding
From playful to serious and cold
From calm to furious and shouting
From distant to proud of his son
qs.why: 처음의 추궁에서 사과와 경청으로 부드러워져요.

qs.q: What is Jin's main emotion when he says "I froze"?
o: Pride in his hard work and results
Anger toward the teacher
Boredom with the subject
Fear of letting his father down
qs.why: 아버지를 실망시킬까 두려웠다고 말해요.

qs.q: What does the father mean by "You could never disappoint me by being human"?
o: Only machines are allowed to make no mistakes at all.
Jin must study harder to become a better person someday.
Making mistakes is natural and will not lower his love.
He is secretly pleased that Jin failed the test today.
qs.why: 실수는 인간적이며 사랑이 줄지 않는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does Jin answer "Fine" at the beginning?
o: He has just passed the test with a high score and wants to hide it.
He wants to avoid talking about something that upset him.
He has not heard his father's question.
He believes his father is not interested.
qs.why: 불편한 이야기를 피하려는 짧은 대답이에요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last line, "eat before the soup gets cold"?
o: To end the tension and show everyday care
To order Jin to leave the table
To complain about the quality of the soup
To change the subject because he is bored
qs.why: 일상적인 말로 분위기를 풀고 배려를 표현해요.

items.title: Great Idea, Really
items.text:
Nora: So I told the manager that I would do all the posters by tomorrow.
Eli: All of them. By tomorrow. Alone.
Nora: Well, yes. How hard can it be?
Eli: Oh, fantastic. And of course you have nothing else to do, like your history project or sleep.
Nora: Are you making fun of me?
Eli: Me? Never. I think it is a wonderful plan. I especially admire the part where it collapses at midnight.
Nora: Okay, I get it. You think I took on too much.
Eli: I think forty posters is a lot for one person. Let me help with the drawing, and you handle the writing.
Nora: Really? You would do that after all your jokes?
Eli: What are friends for? Besides pointing out my own bad ideas, I mean.
Nora: Deal. Thank you.

qs.q: What is the tone of Eli's first remarks ("Oh, fantastic...")?
o: Sincere
Frightened
Admiring
Sarcastic
qs.why: 칭찬하는 척하며 실제로는 계획을 비판하는 빈정거림이에요.

qs.q: What does Eli really think of Nora's plan?
o: It is a wonderful plan that needs no help.
It is unnecessary because there are enough posters.
It is unrealistic for one person to finish alone.
It will be a success within a few hours.
qs.why: 40장을 혼자 하기는 많다고 직접 말해요.

qs.q: How does the conversation end?
o: Nora refuses and leaves angrily.
Eli offers help and Nora accepts gratefully.
Eli decides to stop being friends with Nora.
They agree to cancel the posters.
qs.why: Eli가 그림을 돕겠다고 하고 Nora가 고마워하며 수락해요.

qs.q: What is suggested by Eli's last remark, "Besides pointing out my own bad ideas"?
o: Eli can laugh at himself and has made similar mistakes.
Eli believes he has never had a single bad idea in his life.
Eli wants to blame Nora for mistakes that were really his own.
Eli does not value their friendship as much as Nora does.
qs.why: 자기도 나쁜 계획을 세운 적이 있다는 자기 풍자예요.

items.title: At the Restaurant
items.text:
Waiter: Good evening. Are you ready to order?
Mr. Lee: Actually, I would like to mention something first. I ordered the grilled fish forty minutes ago.
Waiter: I am very sorry, sir. Let me check with the kitchen immediately.
Mr. Lee: I do not mean to cause trouble, but my guests have been waiting, and the other tables around us have already finished.
Waiter: Completely understandable. There was a mix-up with the orders, and that is our fault.
Mr. Lee: I appreciate your honesty. Is there any chance it could be ready in ten minutes?
Waiter: I will make sure of it. In the meantime, may I bring you some bread and a drink, on the house?
Mr. Lee: That is very kind of you. Thank you.
Waiter: Thank you for your patience, sir. I will return shortly.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes Mr. Lee's tone?
o: Rude and shouting
Joking and careless
Fearful and quiet
Polite but firm
qs.why: 불만을 정중하게, 그러나 분명히 말해요.

qs.q: What is the waiter's attitude?
o: Defensive and rather annoyed
Bored and silent
Apologetic and helpful
Proud and boastful
qs.why: 사과하고 해결책을 제시해요.

qs.q: Why does the waiter offer bread and a drink on the house?
o: To tell the guests to leave quickly
To make up for the delay
To advertise the new menu
To collect money from the guests
qs.why: 지연에 대한 보상이에요.

qs.q: What is the main problem in the conversation?
o: Mr. Lee's fish order still has not arrived after a long wait.
The restaurant has run out of fish for the whole evening.
The guests have refused to pay the bill for their meal.
The tables are all full, so no new guests can be seated.
qs.why: 40분이 지나도록 주문이 나오지 않았어요.

items.title: Before the Final
items.text:
Coach: Everybody sit down. Two minutes, then we go out.
Hana: Coach, I do not think I can do this. Their team is so much taller than ours.
Coach: Hana, look at me. How many times did we practice this last week?
Hana: I do not know. Maybe fifty.
Coach: Fifty. And how many times did you miss?
Hana: Not many, I suppose.
Coach: Exactly. You are ready. I did not bring you here to be afraid of a tall team.
Sam: But what if we lose?
Coach: Then we lose together, with our heads high, and we learn. But I do not think that will happen. Play like you did on Tuesday.
Hana: Okay. I will try.
Coach: No. Do not try. Do it. Now, hands in, everyone.

qs.q: What is the coach's tone?
o: Angry and mocking of the players
Nervous and unsure
Bored and impatient
Confident and encouraging
qs.why: 자신감을 주며 격려하는 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the coach ask how many times Hana missed?
o: To scold her for making mistakes
To change the order of players
To remind her that she is well prepared
To find out who should leave the team
qs.why: 연습 성과를 일깨워 자신감을 주려는 거예요.

qs.q: What is Hana's feeling at the beginning?
o: Proud of her team
Worried about the opposing team
Disappointed with the coach's decision
Excited about the match
qs.why: 상대 팀이 크다고 걱정해요.

qs.q: What does the coach mean by "Do not try. Do it"?
o: Hana should act with full commitment instead of doubting herself.
Hana should stay out of the game and watch from the bench.
Hana should practice fifty more times before the final starts.
Hana should stop talking to her teammates until the game ends.

items.title: Planning the Surprise
items.text:
Ravi: Okay, everyone is here. Remember, Ms. Kwon arrives at four, so we have less than an hour.
Mei: I have the banner! It says "Thank you, Ms. Kwon" in four colors.
Ravi: Perfect. Leo, did you bring the cake?
Leo: Um, about that. I left it on the bus.
Ravi: You what?
Leo: Relax, I am joking! It is behind the door. Look at your face!
Mei: That was not funny, Leo. Ravi nearly fainted.
Ravi: I am fine, I am fine. Now, when she opens the door, we all shout together.
Mei: One, two, three, "Surprise!" I can hardly wait to see her smile.
Leo: Quiet, I hear footsteps. Hide, hide!
Ravi: Wait, it is only the janitor. Phew.
Mei: Shhh. The real one is coming. Places, everybody!

qs.q: What is the mood of the conversation?
o: Gloomy and very serious
Calm and sleepy
Angry and hostile
Excited and playful
qs.why: 깜짝 파티를 준비하는 설레고 장난스러운 분위기예요.

qs.q: Why does Ravi react strongly to Leo's remark about the cake?
o: He dislikes Leo's choice of cake.
He wanted to leave the party early.
He believed that the cake was really lost.
He had just won a prize.
qs.why: Leo의 장난을 진짜로 믿고 놀랐어요.

qs.q: What is Leo's attitude when he says "Look at your face!"?
o: Ashamed
Teasing
Respectful
Worried
qs.why: 친구를 놀리는 장난기 어린 태도예요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the group's plan?
o: To thank the teacher with a surprise
To complain to the teacher about the homework
To hold a class election
To prepare for a school exam
qs.why: 선생님께 감사를 전하는 깜짝 파티예요.

items.title: The Phone Call
items.text:
Ms. Berg: Mr. Adams, thank you for taking my call. I am calling about your son, Peter.
Mr. Adams: Is something wrong? He did not come home on time yesterday.
Ms. Berg: Nothing serious, I hope. He missed three classes this week, and I wanted to understand why.
Mr. Adams: Three? I had no idea. He leaves every morning with his bag.
Ms. Berg: I thought as much. Peter is a bright boy, and I do not want to punish him. I want to help.
Mr. Adams: I appreciate that. I will talk to him tonight.
Ms. Berg: If I may suggest, perhaps listen first. Sometimes there is something behind it.
Mr. Adams: You are right. I tend to shout first and ask later.
Ms. Berg: Many of us do. Please call me whenever you wish.
Mr. Adams: Thank you, Ms. Berg. I will.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of Ms. Berg's call?
o: To punish Peter for his bad grades
To invite Mr. Adams to a school festival
To report that Peter won an award
To understand why Peter has been missing classes
qs.why: 결석 이유를 이해하고 돕기 위한 전화예요.

qs.q: How would you describe Ms. Berg's tone?
o: Strict and threatening
Careless and joking
Caring and tactful
Cold and official
qs.why: 벌주기보다 돕고 싶다는 배려 있는 어조예요.

qs.q: How does Mr. Adams feel when he learns about the absences?
o: Delighted and very proud of Peter
Surprised and concerned
Amused and relaxed
Angry at Ms. Berg
qs.why: 3번이나 빠진 줄 몰랐다며 놀라고 걱정해요.

qs.q: What does Mr. Adams admit about himself?
o: He often reacts angrily before listening.
He seldom speaks to his son.
He wants Peter to change schools.
He does not trust teachers.
qs.why: 먼저 소리치고 나중에 묻는 편이라고 인정해요.

items.q:
Which word best describes the tone of this sentence?
"Oh great, another Monday morning meeting. I can hardly contain my excitement."
o: Sarcastic
Sincere
Grateful
Fearful
items.why: 겉으로는 기쁜 척하지만 실제로는 싫다는 빈정거림이에요.

items.q:
Which word best describes the mood created by this sentence?
"The old house stood silent, its dark windows like empty eyes."
o: Cozy
Festive
Humorous
Eerie
items.why: 빈 눈 같은 어두운 창문은 으스스한 분위기를 만들어요.

items.q:
What is the tone of this message?
"Thanks a million for helping me move. I could not have done it without you!"
o: Resentful
Doubtful
Grateful
Gloomy
items.why: 도움에 대한 진심 어린 고마움이 드러나요.

items.q: A sign in a school hallway reads: "Quiet, please. Exams in progress." What is its main purpose?
o: To advertise a school festival
To ask people to be silent
To explain the exam questions
To announce the end of term
items.why: 시험 중이므로 조용히 해 달라는 요청이에요.

items.q: An advertisement says: "Don't miss our summer sale. Everything must go!" What is its purpose?
o: To persuade shoppers to buy
To warn shoppers of danger
To describe how clothes are made
To thank customers for coming
items.why: 구매를 유도하는 광고 문구예요.

items.q: Which sentence is the most formal?
o: Hey, can you send me that file real quick, please?
Send it over to me, would ya, when you get a minute?
Gimme the file now, okay, and don't take too long?
I would be grateful if you could forward the document.
