items.q: Which sentence sounds the most casual?
o: Would you care to join me for lunch later?
I would like to invite you to lunch.
Wanna grab some lunch later?
May I suggest that we have lunch together?
items.why: Wanna는 want to의 구어체로 가장 격의 없어요.

items.q: Which word describes a person who spends money carefully in a positive way?
o: Stingy
Thrifty
Greedy
Wasteful
items.why: thrifty는 알뜰하다는 긍정적 어감이고 stingy는 인색하다는 부정적 어감이에요.

items.q: Which word suggests that someone's confidence has gone too far?
o: Arrogant
Assured
Composed
Determined
items.why: arrogant는 자신감이 지나쳐 거만하다는 부정적 어감이에요.

items.q:
What does "jubilant" mean in this sentence?
"The jubilant crowd threw their hats into the air."
o: Quietly worried
Bitterly disappointed
Very sleepy
Extremely joyful
items.why: jubilant는 매우 기뻐서 환호하는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Which word is closest in meaning to "apprehensive"?
"She felt apprehensive before the interview."
o: Relieved
Furious
Anxious
Amused
items.why: apprehensive는 불안해하는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
What kind of smile is a "sardonic" smile?
"He gave a sardonic smile when he heard the excuse."
o: A warm one
A mocking one
A nervous one
A sleepy one
items.why: sardonic은 비웃는, 냉소적인 뜻이에요.

items.q: Which tone is the most suitable for a speech honoring someone who has died?
o: Solemn and respectful
Playful and teasing
Boastful and loud, with many jokes
Casual and careless
items.why: 추도 연설에는 엄숙하고 존경 어린 어조가 알맞아요.

items.q:
How did Ben feel?
"After hearing the news, Ben was walking on air."
o: Dizzy from illness
Terrified of heights
Ashamed of himself
Delighted
items.why: walking on air는 날아갈 듯 기쁘다는 관용 표현이에요.

items.q:
What does this sentence imply?
"She gave me the cold shoulder at the party."
o: She gave me a cold drink.
She was cold and left early.
She deliberately ignored me.
She hugged me warmly.
items.why: give the cold shoulder는 일부러 무시하다라는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
What does this sentence mean?
"The mood in the room was electric."
o: There was a power failure.
It was full of excitement and tension.
Everyone was sleepy and calm.
The room was very cold and damp.
items.why: electric은 흥분과 긴장이 가득하다는 비유예요.

items.q:
How is the atmosphere described?
"A heavy silence fell over the dinner table."
o: Uncomfortable and tense
Relaxed and cheerful
Busy, noisy, and full of laughter
Fresh and lively
items.why: 무거운 침묵은 어색하고 긴장된 분위기를 나타내요.

items.q: What is the main purpose of an email with the subject line "Reminder: Rent due this Friday"?
o: To invite someone to a wedding
To describe a new apartment
To apologize for a mistake
To remind someone of a payment
items.why: 제목 자체가 납부 기한을 상기시키는 목적을 나타내요.

items.q:
What is the author's most likely purpose in this text?
"A comic story about a cat that gets stuck in a cardboard box and refuses to leave."
o: To give building instructions
To report election results
To entertain readers
To warn about a disease
items.why: 재미있는 이야기의 목적은 독자를 즐겁게 하는 거예요.

items.q:
What does Tim really mean?
"What lovely weather!" said Tim, as rain soaked through his coat.
o: He enjoys getting wet.
The weather is terrible.
He wants to go swimming.
He is looking for his coat.
items.why: 비에 젖으며 말했으므로 반어적 표현이에요.

items.q:
What is the tone of this sentence?
"It's a bit warm," said the man standing in the desert at noon.
o: Humorously understated
Seriously alarmed
Deeply sad
Coldly angry
items.why: 매우 더운 상황을 축소해 말하는 유머러스한 완곡 표현이에요.

items.q: Which sentence creates the most tense mood?
o: Birds sang loudly as the children skipped happily to the park on a sunny morning.
The soup simmered gently while the family laughed together.
Sunlight warmed the garden where the cat slept on a bench.
The clock ticked louder with every second as she waited for the door to open.
items.why: 시계 소리와 기다림이 긴장감을 높여요.

items.q: Which sentence creates the most cheerful mood?
o: The corridor was dark and the floor creaked under his feet.
Rain tapped against the window while the room grew colder.
Laughter filled the kitchen as the family decorated the birthday cake.
No one answered the phone, and the house stayed silent.
items.why: 웃음과 케이크 장식은 즐거운 분위기를 만들어요.

items.q:
What is the attitude of the writer?
"Despite repeated warnings, the company ignored safety rules."
o: Admiring
Critical
Neutral
Amused
items.why: 경고를 무시한 회사를 비판하는 어조예요.

items.q: Which request is the most polite?
o: Could you possibly give me a hand with this?
Help me with this now.
You must help me with this, and you must do it now.
Give me a hand right away.
items.why: Could you possibly는 매우 공손한 요청 표현이에요.

items.q: Which closing is appropriate for a formal business letter?
o: See ya!
Catch you later!
Bye-bye for now!
Yours sincerely,
items.why: Yours sincerely는 격식 있는 편지의 맺음말이에요.

items.q: Which greeting suits a formal letter to a school principal?
o: Hey there, boss,
What's up, Kim?
Dear Principal Kim,
Yo Kim!
items.why: Dear + 직함 + 이름은 격식 있는 편지 인사예요.

items.q:
What is the purpose of this headline?
"SALE: Up to 70% Off This Weekend Only!"
o: To teach a lesson on prices
To attract customers quickly
To praise a famous athlete
To announce a school holiday
items.why: 기간 한정을 강조해 고객의 관심을 끌려는 광고예요.

items.q:
What is the tone of this sentence?
"Under no circumstances should this door be opened."
o: Strict
Playful
Hesitant
Admiring
items.why: 어떤 경우에도 안 된다는 단호한 금지예요.

items.q:
What is the speaker's attitude?
"I suppose it could have been worse," she sighed.
o: Thrilled
Furious
Curious
Resigned
items.why: 한숨과 "worse"는 체념하며 받아들이는 태도를 나타내요.

items.q:
Which feeling does this sentence suggest?
"She stared at the old photograph and smiled sadly."
o: Excitement
Anger and jealousy
Wistfulness
Boredom
items.why: 슬픈 미소는 지난 일을 그리워하는 감정이에요.

items.q:
What does the word "ominous" suggest in this sentence?
"An ominous cloud gathered over the hills."
o: The weather will be perfect.
Something bad may happen soon.
A festival is about to begin.
The hills are very beautiful.
items.why: ominous는 불길한 징조를 뜻해요.

items.q: Which word is closest in meaning to "sincere"?
o: Genuine
Careless
Hidden
Humorous
items.why: sincere는 진심의, genuine과 비슷해요.

items.q: Which word best describes the tone of a bedtime story read in a soft voice?
o: Thrilling
Mocking
Harsh
Soothing
items.why: 부드러운 목소리의 자장가식 이야기는 마음을 달래는 어조예요.

items.q: A writer says a neighbor's promise was "as reliable as a chocolate teapot." What is the tone?
o: Admiring
Neutral
Mocking
Shy
items.why: 초콜릿 찻주전자는 쓸모없다는 뜻으로, 약속을 비웃는 어조예요.

items.q:
What is the purpose of this text?
"First, boil the water. Next, add the noodles and wait three minutes."
o: To tell a funny story
To give instructions
To argue against a rule
To describe a sad memory
items.why: 순서대로 방법을 알려 주는 안내문이에요.

items.q:
What is the writer's tone?
"Our town's festival was a disaster: the rain poured, the band quit, and the food ran out by noon."
o: Disappointed
Delighted
Peaceful
Boastful
items.why: 축제가 엉망이었음을 아쉬워하는 어조예요.

items.q: Which expression shows the speaker is hopeful?
o: "There's no point in trying anymore."
"Nothing ever changes around here."
"I knew it would end badly."
"I'm sure things will get better soon."
items.why: 앞으로 나아질 것이라는 기대를 나타내요.

items.q: A letter ends: "I look forward to hearing from you at your earliest convenience." What is its tone?
o: Rude and demanding
Sad and hopeless
Polite and formal
Excited and childish
items.why: at your earliest convenience는 정중하고 격식 있는 표현이에요.

items.q:
What does the writer want readers to feel?
"Imagine losing your home in a single night, with nothing left but the clothes you wear."
o: Amusement
Sympathy
Pride
Envy
items.why: 상상을 이끌어 독자의 동정심을 유도해요.

items.good: I would be grateful if you could send me the details.
bad: I would be gratitude if you could send me the details.
I would be grateful if you could sending me the details.
I would grateful if you could send me the details.

cz.st: I would be ___ if you could send me the details.

items.rule: 공손한 요청은 would be grateful if you could ~ 형태를 쓰며, be동사 뒤에는 형용사가 와요.

items.good: Had I known about the storm, I would have stayed home.
bad: Had I knew about the storm, I would have stayed home.
Had I known about the storm, I would has stayed home.
Had known I about the storm, I would have stayed home.

cz.st: Had I ___ about the storm, I would have stayed home.

items.rule: if를 생략한 가정법 과거완료는 Had + 주어 + 과거분사로 도치해요.

items.good: Not only was the film long, but it was also dull.
items.ko: 그 영화는 길 뿐만 아니라 지루하기도 했다.
bad: Not only the film was long, but it was also dull.
Not only did the film was long, but it was also dull.
Not only was the film long, but also it dull was.

cz.st: Not only ___ the film long, but it was also dull.

items.rule: Not only가 문장 앞에 오면 주어와 be동사가 도치돼요.

items.good: She sounded as if she were about to cry.
bad: She sounded as if she are about to cry.
She sounded as if she be about to cry.
She sounded like if she were about to cry.

cz.st: She sounded as if she ___ about to cry.

items.rule: as if 뒤에는 가정의 느낌으로 were를 쓸 수 있고, like if는 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The speaker's tone made it clear that he was disappointed.
bad: The speaker's tone made it clearly that he was disappointed.
The speaker's tone made clear it that he was disappointed.
The speaker's tone made it clear what he was disappointed.

cz.st: The speaker's tone made it ___ that he was disappointed.

items.rule: make it + 형용사 + that절 구조에서 목적격 보어 자리에는 형용사를 써요.

items.good: It was such a gloomy day that nobody wanted to go out.
items.ko: 너무 우울한 날이어서 아무도 나가고 싶어 하지 않았다.
bad: It was so a gloomy day that nobody wanted to go out.
It was such gloomy day that nobody wanted to go out.
It was such a gloomy day that nobody didn't want to go out.

cz.st: It was ___ a gloomy day that nobody wanted to go out.

items.rule: such a + 형용사 + 명사 + that ~ 구조예요. so는 형용사 앞에 써요.

items.good: I wish I had spoken more kindly to him.
items.ko: 그에게 더 친절하게 말했더라면 좋았을 텐데.
bad: I wish I have spoken more kindly to him.
I wish I had spoke more kindly to him.
I wish I had speak more kindly to him.

cz.st: I wish I ___ more kindly to him.

items.rule: 과거 사실에 대한 아쉬움은 I wish + had + 과거분사로 표현해요.

items.good: The more she complained, the angrier her boss became.
items.ko: 그녀가 불평할수록 상사는 더 화가 났다.
bad: The more she complained, the more angrier her boss became.
More she complained, the angrier her boss became.
The more she complained, her boss became the angrier.

cz.st: The more she complained, the ___ her boss became.

items.rule: the + 비교급 ~, the + 비교급 ~ 구문이며 angry의 비교급은 angrier예요.

items.good: Although the ending was sad, it felt strangely peaceful.
bad: Although the ending was sad, but it felt strangely peaceful.
Despite the ending was sad, it felt strangely peaceful.
Although the ending was sad, it felt strange peaceful.

cz.st: ___ the ending was sad, it felt strangely peaceful.

items.rule: Although는 절을 이끌고 but과 함께 쓰지 않아요. Despite는 뒤에 명사(구)가 와요.

items.good: She is said to have written the letter in a hurry.
items.ko: 그녀는 서둘러 그 편지를 쓴 것으로 알려져 있다.
bad: She is said have written the letter in a hurry.
She says to have written the letter in a hurry.
She is said to has written the letter in a hurry.

cz.st: She is said to ___ written the letter in a hurry.

items.rule: be said to + have + 과거분사는 이미 일어난 일에 대한 전언을 나타내요.

items.good: Rarely have I felt so relieved.
items.ko: 나는 그렇게 안도한 적이 거의 없다.
bad: Rarely I have felt so relieved.
Rarely have I felt so relieving.
Rarely I felt so relieved.
items.rule: Rarely 같은 부정 부사가 문장 앞에 오면 조동사와 주어가 도치돼요.
